card.summary_ko: 1907년 7월 31일 순종 황제의 이름으로 내려진 군대 해산 조칙으로, 일본의 압력 아래 대한제국군이 해산되고 저항자의 진압을 통감에게 맡겼다. 《순종실록》의 같은 날 기사 가운데 이 조칙만 발췌했다.
card.summary_en: The edict of 31 July 1907, issued in Emperor Sunjong's name, disbanding the Korean army under Japanese pressure and entrusting the suppression of resisters to the Resident-General; an excerpt of that day's Sunjong Veritable Records showing only this edict.
card.edition_ko: 朝鮮王朝實錄/純宗實錄/卽位年 — 중국어 위키문헌, 판 2406155 (7월 31일 군대 해산 조칙만 발췌); 원문은 공문서(저작권법 제7조)로 보호 대상이 아니며, 전사는 위키문헌 기여자(CC BY-SA 4.0)
card.edition_en: 朝鮮王朝實錄/純宗實錄/卽位年 — Chinese Wikisource, revision 2406155 (excerpt: only the 31 July army-disbandment edict); original is an official document outside copyright (Copyright Act art. 7), transcription by Wikisource contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)

notes.ko:
**저자 (발행 주체)** 조칙은 순종 황제(1874–1926, 재위 1907–10)의 이름으로 내려졌다. 순종은 고종이 일본의 압력으로 물러난 뒤 즉위한 황제로, 실권은 거의 없었다. 실제 결정은 이완용 내각이 각의로 하고 통감 이토 히로부미의 요구에 따른 것으로 알려져 있으며, 순종이 망설였다는 기록도 있으나 확실하지 않은 대목이다. 내각은 이완용(총리), 군부대신 이병무 등 이른바 '정미칠적'을 포함하는 친일 성향의 내각이었다. 이 글은 《순종실록》에서 가져온 것인데, 《순종실록》은 1927–32년 이왕직이 조선총독부의 관여 아래 편찬해 일본의 시각이 스며 있다고 비판받는다.

**시대적 맥락** 7월 24일 정미7조약과 함께 작성된 비밀각서에 군대 해산이 포함되어 있었다고 알려져 있다. 일주일 뒤인 7월 31일 이 조칙이 나오고, 다음 날인 8월 1일 훈련원에서 해산식이 열렸다. 시위대 제1연대 제1대대장 박승환이 자결하고 서울 남대문 일대에서 해산에 저항하는 한국군과 일본군 사이에 전투가 벌어졌다. 해산된 군인 가운데 상당수가 의병에 합류해 정미의병이 크게 확산되었다.

**배경** 이 판본은 중국어 위키문헌 「朝鮮王朝實錄/純宗實錄/卽位年」의 7월 31일 항목 가운데 군대 해산 조칙(두 번의 詔曰)만 싣고, 같은 날의 다른 기사들은 뺀 발췌이다. 순종실록의 이 부분은 한문 문장에 한글 토를 단 국한문으로 되어 있고, 고종은 '태황제'로 불린다.

**의의** 대한제국은 이 조칙으로 군대를 잃고 일본에 저항할 군사력을 잃었다. 조칙의 명분은 용병제를 쇄신해 징병제로 바꾸고 사관을 양성한다는 것이었으나, 징병제는 시행되지 않았고 황실 시위에 필요한 인원만 남기고 모두 해산되었다. 조칙 둘째 부분은 해산에 저항하는 이를 진압하는 일을 통감에게 맡기라고 하여, 일본군 개입의 근거가 되었다고 평가된다. 한국에서는 이를 일본의 강요로 본다.

**형식과 주제** 첫 조칙은 한문 문장 사이에 'ᄒᆞ야', 'ᄒᆞ노라', 'ᄂᆞᆫ' 등 한글 토를 단 국한문 혼용체이다. 앞의 이유(재정 절감, 군제 쇄신), 조치(선별 존치와 해산), 은금 지급과 훈계, 그리고 안정 유지를 명하는 두 번째 조칙으로 되어 있다.

**읽기 도움**
- 詔曰(조왈): 조칙에 이르기를
- 朕(짐): 임금이 자신을 가리키는 말
- 傭兵(용병): 고용한 병사
- 徵兵法(징병법): 징병에 관한 법
- 解隊(해대): 부대를 해산함
- 恩金(은금): 은혜로 주는 돈
- 違勅(위칙): 조칙을 어김
- ᄒᆞ야/ᄂᆞᆫ/ᄃᆡ: 하여/는/대
notes.en:
**About the author (issuing authority)** The edict was issued in the name of Emperor Sunjong (1874-1926, reigned 1907-10), who took the throne after Gojong was forced out under Japanese pressure and held almost no real power. The decision is generally understood to have been taken by the Yi Wan-yong cabinet in council at the demand of Resident-General Ito Hirobumi; there are accounts that Sunjong hesitated, but that is not firmly established. The cabinet was pro-Japanese and included Yi Wan-yong as prime minister and Yi Byeong-mu at the Ministry of the Army, among the so-called "Seven Traitors of Jeongmi". The text comes from the Sunjong Veritable Records, which were compiled in 1927-32 by the Yi Household Office under the supervision of the Government-General and are criticised for carrying a Japanese viewpoint.

**Historical context** A secret memorandum made together with the 24 July treaty is said to have included the army's disbandment. A week later, on 31 July, this edict was issued, and on 1 August the disbandment ceremony took place at the Hunryeonwon drill ground. Battalion commander Bak Seung-hwan of the 1st Regiment of the Royal Guard killed himself, and Korean troops resisting disbandment fought Japanese troops in the Namdaemun area of Seoul. Many disbanded soldiers joined the righteous armies and the Jeongmi uprising grew sharply.

**Background** This edition is an excerpt from the 31 July entry of Chinese Wikisource's "朝鮮王朝實錄/純宗實錄/卽位年": only the army-disbandment edict (the two 詔曰 passages) is shown, and the other, unrelated records of the same day are omitted. In this part of the record, Chinese sentences carry Hangul particles, and Gojong is called "Emperor Emeritus".

**Significance** The edict took away the Korean Empire's army and with it its means of resisting Japan. The stated aim was to replace the mercenary system with conscription and to train officers, but no conscription system was introduced and the army was disbanded except for those needed to guard the imperial household. The second part orders the suppression of those who resist to be entrusted to the Resident-General, which is seen as giving a basis for Japanese military intervention. In Korea it is regarded as having been forced by Japan.

**Form and themes** The first edict is in mixed script, Chinese sentences with Hangul endings such as ᄒᆞ야, ᄒᆞ노라, ᄂᆞᆫ. It gives the reasons (saving expenses, military reform), the measures (a selected few retained, the rest disbanded), the payment of gratuities and an admonition, and then a second edict ordering order to be kept.

**Reading help**
- 詔曰: the edict said
- 朕 (jim): "We", the monarch's self-reference
- 傭兵: hired soldiers
- 徵兵法: conscription law
- 解隊: to disband a unit
- 恩金: a gratuity
- 違勅: to defy an edict
- ᄒᆞ야 / ᄂᆞᆫ / ᄃᆡ: modern 하여 / 는 / 대

paragraphs.orig: ○三十一日。詔曰：「朕이惟컨ᄃᆡ國事多艱ᄒᆞᆫ時ᄅᆞᆯ値ᄒᆞ야極히冗費ᄅᆞᆯ節略ᄒᆞ야利用厚生之業에應用ᄒᆞᆷ이今日의急務라。竊惟我現在軍隊ᄂᆞᆮ傭兵으로組成ᄒᆞᆫ故로未足爲上下一致國家完全之防衛일𩭲朕은從今軍制刷新을圖ᄒᆞ야士官養成에專力ᄒᆞ고他日徵兵法을發布ᄒᆞ야鞏固ᄒᆞᆫ兵力을具備코자ᄒᆞᆷ으로朕이玆에有司ᄅᆞᆯ命ᄒᆞ야皇室侍衛에必要ᄒᆞᆫ者ᄅᆞᆯ選置ᄒᆞ고其他ᄂᆞᆮ一時解隊케ᄒᆞ노라。朕은汝等將卒의宿積之勞ᄅᆞᆯ顧念ᄒᆞ야特히隨其階級ᄒᆞ야恩金을頒與ᄒᆞ노니汝等將校下士卒은克體朕意ᄒᆞ야各就其業ᄒᆞ야無愆ᄒᆞᆷ을期ᄒᆞ라。」又詔曰：「軍隊解散時人心動擾치아니토록豫防ᄒᆞ고或違勅暴動者ᄂᆞᆮ鎭壓ᄒᆞᆯ事를統監에게依賴ᄒᆞ라。」
paragraphs.en: On the 31st. An imperial edict said: "We consider that in a time of many national difficulties it is the urgent task of the present day to economise to the utmost on superfluous expenditure and apply the savings to enterprises of using resources and enriching livelihood. Our present army, being composed of hired soldiers, is not sufficient to serve as the complete defence of a state in which high and low are as one. We shall therefore from now on plan a renovation of the military system, devote our efforts to the training of officers, and at a later day promulgate a conscription law and so provide a firm military strength. We therefore hereby command the responsible officials to select and retain those needed for guarding the imperial household, and to disband the rest at once. Bearing in mind the long-accumulated toil of you officers and men, We shall grant to each, according to rank, a gratuity. You officers, non-commissioned officers and soldiers, take well to heart Our intention, and each return to your occupation, taking care to commit no fault." And again an edict said: "So that popular feeling shall not be stirred at the time of the army's disbandment, take precautions beforehand; and entrust to the Resident-General the suppression of any who violate the edict and riot."

review.notes: Trimmed to the heading and the 31 July edict only (three unrelated entries removed); card/edition/notes updated and the now-irrelevant glossary items dropped. Checked translation against the text, the reading character by character (Hangul particles preserved), and notes facts; fixed '이틀 뒤' (it was a week after 24 July) and hedged the claim about Japanese intervention. Secret-memorandum point remains hedged.
